chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'You know my situation, the extent of my generosity, and my willingness to provide for my brothers. So, if I accompany a group of them on the road to Mecca, I can extend my generosity upon them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not do it, O Shihab! If you extend (your generosity) and they extend (their expectations), you will burden them; and if they withhold (their share), you will humble them. Therefore, accompany your equals.'

key_terms.أَجْحَفْتَ بِهِمْ: You would burden them / Aggrieve them

ai.seo_question: Why should one avoid showing off generosity to a group of friends according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih to avoid accompanying peers of unequal financial standing to prevent the social friction of *tajannuf* (partiality) or *idhall* (humiliation). This teaching highlights the Shia ethical emphasis on *mu'asharah* (social conduct) and the psychological impact of economic disparity on dignity, urging believers to choose companionship based on equality to preserve mutual respect.
